report.source_text: After discussions between the interventional radiologist, general surgeon and haematologist, a conservative approach to management was taken. The patient’s old age, moderate frailty and comorbidities favoured conservative treatment, with an interventional approach to be considered if conservative measures were unsuccessful. A total of 6 units of packed red blood cells were transfused over the course of 5 days. Tranexamic acid was also administered during the same time period at a regime of 1 g three times a day. Empirical antibiotic cover was also given. As there was no coagulopathy and a significant interval since the last enoxaparin injection, no reversal agent nor coagulation factors were given. After monitoring for 5 days, the patient’s haemoglobin normalized to 121 g/l. She was subsequently discharged following 5 further days. No routine follow-up was required.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old woman admitted with COVID-19 pneumonitis developed severe abdominal pain, pallor, hypotension, and palpable suprapubic and left iliac fossa masses with visible bruising from enoxaparin injections. Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen and pelvis demonstrated left abdominal wall and pre-peritoneal collections consistent with haematomas and active arterial bleeding from branches of the left inferior epigastric and lumbar arteries, with extension of rectus sheath haematoma dissecting into the extraperitoneal pelvic space. Laboratory testing showed acute anemia (Hb 67 g/l), leukocytosis, and acute kidney injury. A conservative management approach included transfusion of 6 units of packed red blood cells, tranexamic acid administration, and antibiotics; no reversal of anticoagulation was given due to absence of coagulopathy and timing of last enoxaparin dose. Hemoglobin normalized and patient was discharged after clinical improvement.
